entities.summary: Domenico Fattori was a Sammarinese politician who played a pivotal role in shaping San Marino's foreign policy from 1860 to 1908. As Secretary for Foreign Affairs, he navigated the complexities of international relations, forging alliances and negotiating treaties that secured San Marino's independence. Fattori's leadership extended beyond his official duties, as he served as a captain regent of San Marino 12 times between 1857 and 1914, each term contributing to his reputation as a skilled diplomat and statesman. His legacy can be seen in the modern-day diplomatic corps of San Marino, which owes a debt to his vision and expertise. Fattori's commitment to his country's sovereignty and his people's well-being earned him a revered place in Sammarinese history. As captain regent, he worked tirelessly to strengthen San Marino's economy and promote its cultural heritage, leaving a lasting impact on the small country's development. Fattori's influence extended beyond San Marino's borders, as he participated in international gatherings and conferences, advocating for the rights of small nations and promoting peaceful resolution of conflicts. His dedication to his craft and his country has inspired generations of Sammarinese leaders, cementing his position as one of the most important figures in the country's history.
